primitives.name: Tracer
primitives.purpose: Create spans that represent a unit of work, attach attributes and events, link related spans, and propagate context across process and network boundaries.
primitives.api_signature:
from contextlib import AbstractContextManager
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Sequence

class Span(Protocol):
    def set_attribute(self, key: str, value: str | int | float | bool) -> None: ...
    def add_event(self, name: str, attributes: Mapping[str, object] | None = None) -> None: ...
    def record_exception(self, exc: BaseException) -> None: ...
    def set_status(self, code: str, description: str | None = None) -> None: ...

class Tracer(Protocol):
    def start_as_current_span(
        self,
        name: str,
        *,
        kind: str = 'INTERNAL',
        attributes: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
        links: Sequence[object] = (),
    ) -> AbstractContextManager[Span]: ...
    def inject(self, carrier: dict[str, str]) -> None: ...
    def extract(self, carrier: Mapping[str, str]) -> object: ...
invariants: Every span MUST have a non-empty name, a start timestamp, and an end timestamp in that causal order.
A span CANNOT be ended twice; a second end call SHALL be a no-op with a recorded internal warning.
The tracer MUST honor W3C Trace Context headers (traceparent, tracestate) on both inject and extract without mutation of unknown tracestate vendor entries.
Recording an exception MUST set the span status code to ERROR unless the caller explicitly overrides with OK.
Attribute values MUST be one of: string, bool, int, float, or a homogeneous sequence of those types; nested structures are FORBIDDEN.
The tracer SHALL NEVER block the caller waiting for exporter acknowledgement; export is asynchronous.
primitives.extension_contract: A downstream tool extends tracing by registering a SpanProcessor adapter against the TracerProvider; custom attribute semantics are added via a semantic-convention plugin that maps domain keys to OTel attribute names, and context propagation formats are added by registering a TextMapPropagator implementation.
primitives.why_essential: Without a shared tracer contract, each tool emits incompatible span shapes and context headers, breaking cross-service causality and forcing bespoke propagation glue at every network hop.
alternatives_considered: Per-framework tracer (FastAPI-specific decorator) — rejected because propagation breaks at the first out-of-framework hop (worker, CLI, cron).
OpenTracing API — rejected as archived in 2022; its successor OpenTelemetry is the active standard.
Log-only correlation with request_id — rejected because it loses parent/child causality and span timing.

primitives.name: MetricMeter
primitives.purpose: Record numeric measurements through four instrument shapes — counter, up-down counter, histogram, asynchronous gauge — under OpenTelemetry metric semantics.
invariants: Counter instruments MUST only accept non-negative values; negative deltas SHALL raise and are FORBIDDEN to be silently clamped.
Histogram boundaries MUST be finite, strictly increasing, and immutable once the instrument is created.
Instrument names MUST match the regex '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_./-]{0,62}$' per OTel specification and CANNOT collide with a differently-typed instrument of the same name.
Every instrument MUST carry a UCUM unit string (e.g. 'ms', 's', 'By') — an empty unit is FORBIDDEN.
Observable gauge callbacks MUST be idempotent within a collection cycle and SHALL NEVER raise; exceptions are logged and the measurement is dropped.
Attribute sets attached to measurements NEVER include unbounded-cardinality keys (user id, request id, full URL path).
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools register a MetricReader adapter (pull-based Prometheus scrape or push-based OTLP exporter) and extend instrumentation by subclassing the meter provider to add a View that renames, filters, or re-aggregates instruments without mutating existing instrument contracts.

sources.locator: https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/ 'When to use which' and 'Errors of quantile estimation'

primitives.why_essential: Centralizing instrument creation is the only way to keep units, names, and attribute sets aligned across services; ad-hoc per-tool meters silently fork names and aggregations, making dashboards non-portable.
alternatives_considered: StatsD client per tool — rejected because it has no unit or description metadata and offers no histogram bucket control.
Prometheus client library directly — rejected because it binds code to pull-only collection and blocks push-based deployment models.
Pure log-derived metrics — rejected because aggregation at ingest is costly and loses millisecond-resolution histograms.

primitives.name: StructuredLogger
primitives.purpose: Emit machine-parseable key/value log records with a fixed level taxonomy, attached trace and span identifiers, and no positional string formatting.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Any

class StructuredLogger(Protocol):
    def debug(self, event: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...
    def info(self, event: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...
    def warn(self, event: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...
    def error(self, event: str, *, exc: BaseException | None = None, **fields: Any) -> None: ...
    def bind(self, **fields: Any) -> 'StructuredLogger': ...
    def with_context(self, context: Mapping[str, Any]) -> 'StructuredLogger': ...
invariants: Every emitted record MUST be a single line of valid UTF-8 JSON with keys 'ts', 'level', 'event', plus the caller-provided fields.
Log level SHALL be one of DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR; TRACE and FATAL are FORBIDDEN to prevent drift from OTel log severity ranges.
When a span is active in the current context, the record MUST automatically include 'trace_id' and 'span_id' in hex form.
Printf-style formatting with %s or f-strings inside the event message is FORBIDDEN; values ALWAYS travel as typed fields.
Secrets matching registered redaction patterns (authorization headers, bearer tokens, card PANs) MUST be replaced with '[REDACTED]' before serialization.
Binding a field NEVER mutates the parent logger; bind returns a new immutable logger instance.
primitives.extension_contract: A downstream tool plugs in a redaction filter via the register-processor hook, adds custom severity-to-sink routing by composing a WriteAdapter, or injects static fields (service.version, git.sha) through a bound child logger that decorators and middleware receive as dependency.

sources.locator: Chapter 3 'Lessons from Scaling Without Observability' pp. 32-38 on structured events

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 6 'Monitoring Distributed Systems' section 'Logs vs Metrics'

primitives.why_essential: A shared logger is the only way to guarantee every record is parseable by the same ingest pipeline and automatically carries trace correlation; per-tool loggers forget to inject span context and produce grep-friendly-but-query-hostile prose.
alternatives_considered: Python stdlib logging with a JSON formatter — rejected because the default API encourages positional formatting and loses types at the boundary.
Per-service print statements + log shipper — rejected because line parsing is fragile and trace correlation becomes post-hoc regex.
Binary structured logging (protobuf) — rejected because debuggability in production terminals requires human-readable output.

primitives.name: CorrelationContext
primitives.purpose: Propagate a stable request identifier and optional baggage across threads, async tasks, and network hops so every downstream record can be joined back to the originating request.
invariants: The request_id MUST be a lowercase hex or ULID string of at least 16 characters and SHALL be stable for the entire request lifecycle.
Baggage values MUST be ASCII and each individual value CANNOT exceed 8192 bytes per W3C Baggage specification.
Activating a context MUST restore the prior context on exit even if an exception is raised.
When extracting from headers, an invalid traceparent value SHALL cause a new trace id to be generated and NEVER falls back to an empty trace context.
Baggage keys reserved for authentication (password, authorization, cookie) are FORBIDDEN and SHALL be stripped on ingest.
CorrelationContext NEVER leaks across event loops; asynchronous task spawns copy-on-capture the current context via contextvars.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools register a middleware that extracts the context from inbound transport headers (HTTP, gRPC, SQS message attributes) and compose a propagator adapter that re-injects the context into outbound calls; baggage keys are extended by registering a namespaced key prefix through the bind method.
primitives.consumption_example:
async def enqueue_job(ctx: CorrelationContext, payload: dict, queue) -> None:
    headers = dict(ctx.to_headers())
    headers['x-request-id'] = ctx.request_id
    await queue.send(body=payload, attributes=headers)
    current = CorrelationContext.current()
    assert current.request_id == ctx.request_id

sources.locator: Chapter 4 'How Observability and Monitoring Come Together' pp. 48-52 on request-scoped context

primitives.why_essential: Without a single correlation primitive, each layer invents its own header (X-Request-Id, X-Trace-Id, X-Correlation) and async boundaries drop context silently, making end-to-end reconstruction impossible.
alternatives_considered: Thread-local storage — rejected because it does not survive async/await task switches in Python asyncio.
Manually threading the context through every function signature — rejected because it does not survive framework callbacks and middleware.
Attaching context only to the root span — rejected because logs emitted outside the span (startup, shutdown, background tasks) lose correlation.

primitives.name: ErrorSink
primitives.purpose: Capture uncaught exceptions with fingerprint grouping, attach current trace and correlation context, apply sampling, and forward to an error-tracking backend.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Callable

class ErrorSink(Protocol):
    def capture_exception(
        self,
        exc: BaseException,
        *,
        level: str = 'error',
        tags: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        extras: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
    ) -> str: ...
    def capture_message(self, message: str, *, level: str = 'error', tags: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> str: ...
    def register_fingerprinter(self, fn: Callable[[BaseException], list[str]]) -> None: ...
    def before_send(self, fn: Callable[[dict], dict | None]) -> None: ...
invariants: Every captured event MUST include the active trace_id, span_id, and request_id when any of those are set.
A fingerprint MUST be deterministic for the same exception type plus top-three stack frames; otherwise identical incidents SHALL NEVER split into separate issues.
capture_exception MUST redact registered PII field names (email, password, authorization) before transport.
The sink CANNOT block the caller; serialization and network transmission SHALL run on a background worker.
before_send hooks returning None MUST drop the event and NEVER partially transmit it.
Sampling SHALL apply AFTER fingerprinting so rare variants are not accidentally suppressed by head-of-queue drops.
primitives.extension_contract: Tools extend the sink by registering a fingerprinter callable that returns a list of grouping keys, by registering a before_send filter that redacts or drops events, and by implementing a TransportAdapter that speaks the target vendor's envelope while preserving the neutral event payload.

sources.locator: Chapter 5 'Structured Events Are the Building Blocks of Observability' pp. 57-62

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 6 section 'Four Golden Signals' on error-rate grouping

primitives.why_essential: Per-tool error handling drops trace context and produces duplicate issues; one sink with fingerprinting and context-attachment is the only way to keep error groups stable and joinable to the originating trace.
alternatives_considered: Relying on log aggregation for errors — rejected because log pipelines lack fingerprint-based grouping and alert fatigue follows.
Per-framework exception middleware — rejected because background jobs, CLI, and consumers fall outside framework boundaries.
Raw stacktrace hashing as the only fingerprint — rejected because line-number drift from refactors splits stable issues.

primitives.name: SamplingPolicy
primitives.purpose: Decide whether a given trace or span is retained, combining head-based (at span start) and tail-based (post hoc) rules and honoring the parent sampling decision.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Sequence

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SamplingDecision:
    sampled: bool
    attributes: Mapping[str, str]
    trace_state: str | None

class SamplingPolicy(Protocol):
    def should_sample(
        self,
        *,
        parent_context: object | None,
        trace_id: str,
        name: str,
        kind: str,
        attributes: Mapping[str, object],
        links: Sequence[object],
    ) -> SamplingDecision: ...
    def description(self) -> str: ...
invariants: When a parent span carries the sampled flag, child spans MUST inherit that decision unless the policy explicitly declares itself parent-overriding.
The sampling decision SHALL be deterministic for the same trace_id so that siblings agree without coordination.
Probabilistic sampling MUST use the trace_id hash modulo a rate, NEVER a per-span random draw, to keep entire traces intact.
Policies CANNOT raise; a failing policy SHALL fall back to the default deny and emit an internal counter increment.
Tail-based sampling decisions MUST NOT retroactively modify already-exported spans; they ALWAYS run before export buffering flushes.
description() returns a stable, human-readable string that NEVER includes secret keys or cardinality-exploding values.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools compose a new policy by implementing the SamplingPolicy protocol and register it with the TracerProvider; composite policies chain via the compose adapter (latency-threshold OR error-seen OR head-probability) and trace-state propagation is preserved by returning the caller's trace_state unmodified when undecided.

sources.locator: Chapter 17 'Cheap and Accurate Enough: Sampling' pp. 207-220

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems

primitives.why_essential: Ingest cost scales with trace volume; without a coherent policy primitive, tools each invent their own drop rules and break the property that a trace is retained or dropped as a whole.
alternatives_considered: 100% sampling — rejected because storage and egress costs grow linearly with traffic without a bounded slope.
Random per-span sampling — rejected because it shatters traces into partial subtrees that cannot be reconstructed.
Client-side header-only sampling — rejected because error-only and latency-only decisions require span-time or post-hoc evaluation.

primitives.name: SemanticAttributes
primitives.purpose: Expose the OpenTelemetry semantic-convention attribute keys as typed constants and enforce that primitives populate required keys for HTTP, database, messaging, and GenAI operations.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Final

class SemanticAttributes:
    SERVICE_NAME: Final[str] = 'service.name'
    SERVICE_VERSION: Final[str] = 'service.version'
    DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT: Final[str] = 'deployment.environment.name'
    HTTP_REQUEST_METHOD: Final[str] = 'http.request.method'
    HTTP_ROUTE: Final[str] = 'http.route'
    HTTP_RESPONSE_STATUS_CODE: Final[str] = 'http.response.status_code'
    DB_SYSTEM: Final[str] = 'db.system'
    DB_STATEMENT: Final[str] = 'db.statement'
    MESSAGING_SYSTEM: Final[str] = 'messaging.system'
    MESSAGING_DESTINATION_NAME: Final[str] = 'messaging.destination.name'
    GEN_AI_SYSTEM: Final[str] = 'gen_ai.system'
    GEN_AI_REQUEST_MODEL: Final[str] = 'gen_ai.request.model'
    GEN_AI_USAGE_INPUT_TOKENS: Final[str] = 'gen_ai.usage.input_tokens'
    GEN_AI_USAGE_OUTPUT_TOKENS: Final[str] = 'gen_ai.usage.output_tokens'
invariants: Attribute keys MUST match the lowercase dotted notation specified by OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions 1.27 and SHALL NEVER be aliased to custom names.
Required keys for a given domain (http.request.method for HTTP server spans, db.system for DB spans) MUST be populated before a span ends.
Values for enum attributes (db.system, messaging.system) MUST come from the SemConv registry and CANNOT be free-form strings.
Deprecated keys SHALL be aliased to the current key with a one-time warning, NEVER silently dropped.
The full SQL statement under db.statement MUST be redacted when the deployment environment is production; literal parameter values are FORBIDDEN.
SemanticAttributes class keys are immutable class attributes and NEVER reassigned at runtime.
primitives.extension_contract: New domains extend the attribute set by subclassing SemanticAttributes and adding Final-typed constants that track a specific semconv version; the subclass is bound to a namespace via register() so linting tools can enforce that domain spans carry the subclass's required keys.
primitives.consumption_example:
def annotate_http_span(span, method: str, route: str, status: int) -> None:
    span.set_attribute(SemanticAttributes.HTTP_REQUEST_METHOD, method)
    span.set_attribute(SemanticAttributes.HTTP_ROUTE, route)
    span.set_attribute(SemanticAttributes.HTTP_RESPONSE_STATUS_CODE, status)
primitives.why_essential: Shared keys are what make traces, metrics, and logs from different services joinable in a backend; without a single source of attribute names, every team invents 'httpMethod' vs 'http_method' and queries fragment.
alternatives_considered: Free-form string keys — rejected because every team spells the same concept differently and dashboards cannot be shared.
Per-tool attribute modules — rejected because they drift from upstream semconv updates and miss required-key enforcement.
OpenTracing tag taxonomy — rejected because it was frozen in 2019 and lacks HTTP, DB, messaging, and GenAI coverage.

primitives.name: CardinalityGuard
primitives.purpose: Bound the unique attribute-value combinations attached to a metric or log stream to prevent label explosion from breaking time-series databases.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Mapping

class CardinalityGuard(Protocol):
    def admit(self, metric_name: str, attributes: Mapping[str, str]) -> Mapping[str, str]: ...
    def configure(self, *, per_metric_limit: int, per_key_limit: int, overflow_label: str = 'overflow') -> None: ...
    def stats(self, metric_name: str) -> Mapping[str, int]: ...
invariants: When the per-metric series limit is reached, new attribute combinations MUST be collapsed into a single 'overflow' series and NEVER emitted with their original values.
The guard MUST reject any attribute key whose value has been seen in more than per_key_limit distinct forms across the window.
User identifiers, full URL paths, email addresses, and freeform query strings as attribute values are FORBIDDEN by the default deny-list.
Admission decisions SHALL be deterministic given the same (metric_name, attributes) tuple within a single aggregation window.
The guard NEVER mutates the caller's attribute mapping in place; it ALWAYS returns a new mapping.
Overflow events MUST be observable through a dedicated counter so operators can detect label pressure before ingestion breaks.
Configure CANNOT be invoked after the first admit call in a given process to preserve deterministic behavior.
primitives.extension_contract: Teams extend the guard by registering a domain-specific key classifier (e.g. an adapter that maps user_id → 'uid_redacted'), by composing a deny-list plugin that supplements the default patterns, and by subclassing the guard to emit overflow events to a custom TelemetrySink.
primitives.consumption_example:
def record_request(meter: MetricMeter, guard: CardinalityGuard, route: str, user_id: str, status: int) -> None:
    hist = meter.histogram('http.server.duration', unit='ms', description='HTTP latency')
    safe_attrs = guard.admit('http.server.duration', {'http.route': route, 'user.id': user_id, 'http.response.status_code': str(status)})
    hist.record(12.4, safe_attrs)
    assert 'user.id' not in safe_attrs or safe_attrs['user.id'] == 'overflow'

sources.locator: https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/instrumentation/ section 'Do not overuse labels' and 'Cardinality is hard'
Chapter 1 'What Is Observability?' pp. 8-12 on high-cardinality data and its costs
specification/metrics/sdk.md section 'View' on attribute filtering and aggregation selection

primitives.why_essential: A single unbounded label (user id, raw URL) can 10x a metrics bill overnight and make dashboards unqueryable; without a shared guard primitive, each tool ships its own footgun.
alternatives_considered: Relying on operators to audit dashboards — rejected because the blast radius lands in production before review.
Per-metric hardcoded allowlists — rejected because coverage drifts as new instruments are added.
Downstream TSDB-side label limits — rejected because by the time the TSDB refuses the write, the agent buffer and network have already paid the cost.

primitives.name: HistogramBuckets
primitives.purpose: Define explicit latency and size bucket boundaries for histogram instruments so quantile estimation is accurate and comparable across services.
invariants: Boundaries MUST be strictly increasing, finite, non-negative, and SHALL include at least five buckets below the target p99.
Once assigned to an instrument, boundaries are immutable; changing them at runtime is FORBIDDEN because it invalidates historical quantile comparisons.
Latency boundaries MUST be expressed in milliseconds with unit 'ms' and NEVER mixed with seconds on the same instrument.
The lowest boundary MUST be smaller than the realistic floor of the measured distribution so the first bucket is not saturated.
Bucket count SHALL NOT exceed 20 per instrument to bound per-series storage cost.
Default bucket sets for HTTP latency and payload size MUST be derived from the OpenTelemetry HTTP semconv recommendation and CANNOT be silently overridden at instrument creation.
primitives.extension_contract: Tools extend the defaults by registering a named bucket preset (e.g. 'db.query.latency', 'llm.completion.latency') through a HistogramProvider adapter; callers bind a preset to an instrument at creation time, and the preset carries version metadata so dashboards can detect a boundary change.
primitives.consumption_example:
def checkout_latency(meter: MetricMeter) -> None:
    preset = HistogramBuckets.latency_ms_default()
    instrument = meter.histogram(preset.name, unit=preset.unit, description='checkout latency', boundaries=preset.boundaries)
    instrument.record(34.5, {'checkout.step': 'payment'})
    assert preset.unit == 'ms'

sources.locator: https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/ 'Errors of quantile estimation' and default bucket guidance

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 6 section 'Four Golden Signals' on latency bucket selection

primitives.why_essential: Heterogeneous bucket boundaries make p99 numbers across services non-comparable; sharing a bucket primitive is how every dashboard stops lying about tail latency.
alternatives_considered: Exponential histogram (HDR style) — rejected as of 2026 because backend support is still uneven; retained as an emerging opt-in.
Summary quantiles computed client-side — rejected because they cannot be aggregated across instances without error.
Per-service ad-hoc buckets — rejected because cross-service comparison is a required SRE operation.

primitives.name: ResourceDescriptor
primitives.purpose: Describe the entity producing telemetry — service, version, deployment environment, instance id — and attach that identity to every span, metric, and log record.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Mapping

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ResourceDescriptor:
    service_name: str
    service_namespace: str | None
    service_version: str
    service_instance_id: str
    deployment_environment: str
    attributes: Mapping[str, str]

    def merged_with(self, overrides: Mapping[str, str]) -> 'ResourceDescriptor': ...
    def to_attributes(self) -> Mapping[str, str]: ...
invariants: service.name MUST be non-empty; a missing service.name SHALL cause telemetry initialization to fail fast rather than emit 'unknown_service'.
service.instance.id MUST be unique per running process and SHALL be stable for the lifetime of that process.
deployment.environment.name MUST be one of a declared enum (development / staging / production / preview) and free-form values are FORBIDDEN.
The resource descriptor is immutable after construction; merged_with ALWAYS returns a new descriptor.
Attribute values injected through to_attributes MUST use the canonical semconv keys (service.name, not serviceName).
The descriptor NEVER contains secrets, credentials, or personally identifiable data.
primitives.extension_contract: Platforms extend resource detection by registering a ResourceDetector plugin (Kubernetes, ECS, Lambda) that contributes additional semconv-compliant attributes; the merge adapter resolves conflicts by giving explicit configuration priority over auto-detected values.
primitives.consumption_example:
def build_resource() -> ResourceDescriptor:
    desc = ResourceDescriptor(
        service_name='checkout',
        service_namespace='payments',
        service_version='2026.04.3',
        service_instance_id='pod-abc-123',
        deployment_environment='production',
        attributes={'cloud.provider': 'aws', 'cloud.region': 'us-east-1'},
    )
    return desc

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems

primitives.why_essential: Without a shared resource primitive, the same service reports under three different names across exporters, and dashboards cannot aggregate by environment; identity is the glue of every multi-service query.
alternatives_considered: Attaching service.name at each span call site — rejected because it bloats instrumentation and drifts across modules.
Environment variables consumed ad hoc by each tool — rejected because typing, validation, and drift detection are missing.
Kubernetes downward API alone — rejected because non-Kubernetes environments (Lambda, ECS, bare metal) require distinct detectors.

primitives.name: TelemetryExporter
primitives.purpose: Serialize batched spans, metrics, or log records into an OTLP-compatible envelope and deliver them to a configured endpoint with retry and backpressure.
primitives.api_signature:
from enum import Enum
from typing import Protocol, Sequence

class Signal(str, Enum):
    TRACES = 'traces'
    METRICS = 'metrics'
    LOGS = 'logs'

class ExportResult(str, Enum):
    SUCCESS = 'success'
    FAILURE = 'failure'
    TIMEOUT = 'timeout'

class TelemetryExporter(Protocol):
    signal: Signal

    def export(self, batch: Sequence[object], *, timeout_s: float) -> ExportResult: ...
    def force_flush(self, *, timeout_s: float) -> bool: ...
    def shutdown(self, *, timeout_s: float) -> bool: ...
invariants: Exporter calls MUST be non-blocking on the hot path; the caller SHALL always enqueue through an intermediate batch processor.
On transient failure the exporter MUST retry with exponential backoff, capped at a configurable maximum, and NEVER retry indefinitely.
Shutdown MUST flush the in-flight batch within the provided timeout and CANNOT accept new export calls afterwards.
The wire format MUST conform to OTLP/HTTP protobuf or OTLP/gRPC as defined by OpenTelemetry Specification 1.32.
Authentication headers attached to exports are FORBIDDEN from appearing in any log record, span attribute, or error event emitted by the exporter itself.
Export results SHALL be observable via an internal counter keyed by (signal, result) so operators can alert on sustained failure.
primitives.extension_contract: A backend adapter implements the TelemetryExporter Protocol for its wire format, registers itself with the signal-specific provider, and is composed behind a BatchSpanProcessor / PeriodicExportingMetricReader so batching and retry semantics are preserved independently of the adapter.

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 6 section 'Setting Reasonable Expectations for Monitoring' on exporter reliability

primitives.why_essential: Batching, retry, backpressure, and authentication are non-trivial and must not be reinvented per tool; one exporter primitive keeps the hot path cheap and the failure mode predictable.
alternatives_considered: Direct synchronous writes from the hot path — rejected because any network hiccup becomes tail-latency for end users.
Vendor-native SDKs only — rejected because they couple code to a single backend and block multi-destination fan-out.
File-based export + sidecar forwarder — rejected as a primary path because disk-queue management belongs in infra, not in-process.

primitives.name: AuditEvent
primitives.purpose: Emit a tamper-evident, append-only record of a security-relevant action with actor, subject, action verb, outcome, and a cryptographic chain link.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Mapping, Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AuditEvent:
    event_id: str
    occurred_at: datetime
    actor_id: str
    actor_type: str
    action: str
    resource_type: str
    resource_id: str
    outcome: str
    attributes: Mapping[str, str]
    prev_hash: str
    event_hash: str

class AuditEventSink(Protocol):
    def emit(self, event: AuditEvent) -> None: ...
    def verify_chain(self, from_event_id: str | None = None) -> bool: ...
invariants: event_hash MUST be computed as SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of all non-hash fields concatenated with prev_hash; a mismatched hash SHALL invalidate the chain.
Once emitted, an AuditEvent is append-only and CANNOT be updated, deleted, or logically superseded.
outcome MUST be one of 'success', 'failure', 'denied'; any other value is FORBIDDEN to keep reporting queryable.
actor_id MUST be set even for system-initiated actions; 'system' is a reserved literal and NEVER empty.
occurred_at MUST be an absolute UTC timestamp with at least millisecond precision; naive timestamps are FORBIDDEN.
action verbs MUST come from a controlled vocabulary (CREATE / READ / UPDATE / DELETE / GRANT / REVOKE / EXPORT) and ALWAYS use that controlled set for cross-system joins.
primitives.extension_contract: Domains extend the vocabulary by registering a namespaced action prefix (e.g. 'payment.refund') through an AuditVocabulary provider; sinks are added by implementing AuditEventSink and composing them into a FanOutSink so WORM storage, SIEM, and warm-query stores each receive the same stream.
primitives.consumption_example:
def record_user_export(sink, actor: str, user_id: str, prev_hash: str) -> AuditEvent:
    from hashlib import sha256
    from datetime import datetime, timezone
    event_id = 'evt_01J9ZX'
    canonical = f'{event_id}|{actor}|user|EXPORT|{user_id}|success|{prev_hash}'
    evt = AuditEvent(
        event_id=event_id,
        occurred_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
        actor_id=actor,
        actor_type='human',
        action='EXPORT',
        resource_type='user',
        resource_id=user_id,
        outcome='success',
        attributes={'reason': 'dsar'},
        prev_hash=prev_hash,
        event_hash=sha256(canonical.encode()).hexdigest(),
    )
    sink.emit(evt)
    return evt

sources.locator: Section 3.2 'Infrastructure for Log Management' and 3.3 'Log Analysis'
Chapter 14 'Observability and the Software Supply Chain' pp. 173-178 on audit records

primitives.why_essential: Regulated domains (SOC2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) require a verifiable audit trail that per-tool loggers cannot produce; the hash chain is what distinguishes audit from logging and it must be enforced centrally.
alternatives_considered: Reusing StructuredLogger for audit — rejected because logs are mutable at the pipeline level and lack a tamper-evident chain.
Database row CRUD history — rejected because it captures state deltas, not actor intent or denied actions.
External SIEM-only ingestion — rejected because the SIEM becomes the source of truth and proof-of-intent is delegated offsite.

cross_cutting_insights: Traces, metrics, and logs are three projections of the same structured event; every primitive here assumes they share service.name, trace_id, and timestamp so backends can join them without post-hoc glue.

Every signal carries the same identity: ResourceDescriptor plus CorrelationContext appear in Tracer, MetricMeter, StructuredLogger, ErrorSink, and AuditEvent — identity is not per-signal, it is per-process.

Cardinality is the single biggest operational footgun; CardinalityGuard, SemanticAttributes enum values, and SamplingPolicy each attack a different vector (labels, keys, volume) of the same failure mode.
Asynchronous export is mandatory across the board — Tracer, MetricMeter, ErrorSink, and TelemetryExporter all forbid blocking the hot path because production traffic cannot pay for collector latency.
Semantic conventions 1.27 is the interface contract between instrumentation code and analysis tools; any primitive that invents its own attribute names defeats the purpose of portable telemetry.

Sampling decisions must be trace-coherent, not span-local — SamplingPolicy, Tracer context propagation, and TelemetryExporter batching all rely on the invariant that an entire trace is kept or dropped as a unit.

Audit and observability share primitives but diverge on mutability — AuditEvent is append-only and chain-verified, while spans and metrics are best-effort and lossy; conflating them is a compliance failure.
gaps_observed: SKILL-001 lacks a dedicated Tracer primitive — spans are created ad hoc per tool and propagation across Celery/arq workers is not enforced.
No CardinalityGuard equivalent exists; metric attribute sets are free-form and user_id-like keys can reach the TSDB uncapped.
Error capture is coupled to request middleware, so background jobs, scheduled tasks, and CLI entrypoints emit errors without trace_id.
SemanticAttributes keys are not centralized — HTTP and DB spans use inconsistent keys across generators, blocking cross-service queries.
There is no SamplingPolicy primitive; sampling is either all-or-nothing at the exporter level and cannot keep error traces selectively.
AuditEvent exists in audit tools but does not enforce a hash-chain invariant, so tamper evidence depends on downstream WORM storage.
ResourceDescriptor detection is manual; Kubernetes and AWS auto-detectors are not wired into the default telemetry bootstrap.
HistogramBuckets presets are hardcoded per tool, so p99 comparisons across checkout, payments, and auth latencies are not apples-to-apples.
